0.7.4 is a drop-in patch for 0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.7.2 and 0.7.3: format epoch 3 is unchanged, with no storage, snapshot, WAL or Raft protocol change. Upgrade in place with an ordinary rolling restart (`helm upgrade`). No fresh install or data move is needed.

- **Gateway metrics and the upgrade.** A gateway with access control (`--auth-issuer`) now answers `404` on `/__ursula/gateway/metrics` ([#548](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/548)). If something scrapes that path, add `--auth-public-metrics` to `gateway.extraArgs` in the same `helm upgrade` that moves the gateways to 0.7.4, and remove it before rolling a gateway back to an earlier release, because a gateway before 0.7.4 exits at startup on the unknown flag. The flag makes the counters public. From 0.7.0, a values file that pins `global.image.tag` or `gateway.image.tag` must move it together with the chart, as for 0.7.1, and from 0.7.2 or earlier the 0.7.3 upgrade notes apply too.
- **Snapshot builds escalate before the Raft log hard limit** ([#519](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/519)). At or past `raft.snapshot_log_budget` a node runs more snapshot builds at once the further its log is past the budget, up to `raft.snapshot_build_max_concurrency`, whose default rises from 1 to 2, and a pass starts up to `raft.snapshot_pressure_max_groups_per_tick` groups for each build it keeps in flight. With the snapshot sizes of #519, two builds hold about 11 MB in the common case, about 270 MB for two of the largest groups and about 400 MB if both fall back to inline snapshots. Setting `raft.snapshot_build_max_concurrency` to 1 keeps one build at a time and is safe at any time. Set a value above 1 only after every node runs 0.7.4, because servers before 0.7.4 read it too and a `helm upgrade` changes the chart's ConfigMap in place: an older pod that restarts before the rollout replaces it then runs up to that many builds at once at any log level, which was never validated. The chart renders it only when `raft.snapshotBuildMaxConcurrency` is set, so with it unset a server before 0.7.4 keeps its default of 1. With the snapshot driver off (`storage.snapshot.drive_interval = 0`), OpenRaft's own policy may now run two builds at once too. On a 3-voter test cluster with real S3 and 128 SQLite VFS owners writing flat out, 0.7.3, and 0.7.4 set to one build, crossed the hard limit on every node, while the default of 2 stayed well below it. Of the existing metrics, only `raft_snapshot_pressure_passes` changed meaning.
- **An operator's snapshot waits for a build permit** ([#529](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/529)). `POST /__ursula/raft/{group}/snapshot` waits while a build of the group runs and while other builds hold every snapshot build permit, answers `200` when a snapshot covers what the group had applied when the request arrived, and answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1` when no build of the group can start within 10 s, where it answered `500` after about 10 s. A request can now take up to about 20 s, 10 s for a build to start and 10 s for its snapshot. A build of the group that has just ended can go unseen for a moment, so the request may start another build ([#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561)).
- **Refusals the gateway decides from the request head reach clients that send the body first** ([#540](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/540)). Before a `401`, `403`, `404`, `429` or one of its `503`s for an unavailable token issuer or authorizer, the gateway reads and discards the body, stopping after 5 s without new data or 30 s in all. A body declared or read over `--max-request-body-bytes` still gets the refusal, and the connection closes. A large SQLite VFS commit refused this way now fails alone instead of poisoning the database. A refused upload costs the gateway its ingress.
- **The SQLite VFS is no longer experimental.** Within a minor release the formats stay compatible, but a patch release can still change the API, as 0.7.3 did, and the release notes say how to upgrade.
- **SQLite VFS: a commit whose attempts never went out fails alone**, with `refused_kind` `unreachable` and its producer sequence free, instead of poisoning the database. The extension caches host addresses for 30 s and keeps the last ones for up to 10 minutes while lookups fail. The request that looks a host up waits for the lookup, up to 5 s, even with a pooled connection ready. On macOS the extension retries a reset reported as `Invalid argument (os error 22)` ([#542](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/542)). TypeScript's `WriteRefusedKind` gains `unreachable`.
- **Rust library APIs changed** in `ursula-raft` (`SnapshotBuildCoordinator`, `SnapshotStartError` and `snapshot_cadence`), `ursula-runtime` (`RuntimeMetrics` and `RuntimeMetricsSnapshot`), `ursula-gateway` (`AccessControl::with_public_metrics`) and `ursula-config` (the default of `snapshot_build_max_concurrency`), with no wire or on-disk change.

Known issues: [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#452](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/452), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#484](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/484), [#490](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/490), [#492](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/492), [#494](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/494), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#497](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/497), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#539](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/539), [#550](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/550) and [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561). Every change is listed in the [0.7.4 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#074).
